chunks: As for what Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Jaʿfar ibn Bashir al-Bajali, from Hammad ibn ʿUthman, from ʿAmmar ibn Musa, who said:
I heard Aba ʿAbd Allah عليه السلام say: If a man forgets to perform istinja' after defecation until he prays, he does not repeat the salat (prayer).

The correct way to understand this report is that he forgot to perform istinja' with water, though he had performed istinja' with stones. If that is the case, repeating the salat (prayer) is not required of him. What has preceded from the reports indicates this, and it further clarifies the matter.

key_terms.إِعَادَةُ: repetition, here meaning repeating the salat (prayer)
key_terms.الْأَخْبَارِ: reports, i.e. hadith narrations used as evidence
key_terms.الْغَائِطِ: defecation; the state requiring post-relief cleansing
key_terms.بِالْأَحْجَارِ: with stones, meaning cleansing with stones as a valid form of istinja'
key_terms.يَسْتَنْجِيَ: to perform istinja', cleansing oneself after relieving oneself

ai.seo_question: Does someone need to repeat salat (prayer) if he forgot istinja' with water after defecation?
ai.summary: This report discusses a legal ruling concerning ritual purity and salat (prayer). It explains that if a person had already cleansed himself with stones after relieving himself and only forgot washing with water, then his salat (prayer) does not need to be repeated.
